# LASSO: An LLM-Agent Synthesized System for SQL Validation

[All reading notes](../reading-notes.md) · [Catalog entry](../README.md#lasso)

**Full paper read · 2026-11-09**

[Original source](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.38294v1) · arXiv:2610.38294v1, 28 October 2026; manuscript retains placeholder PVLDB citation fields

**Reading coverage:** All 13 pages: sections 1–7, agent-development process, data-generator/attack strategies, normalization/comparison rules, all eight result tables and references.

## Research question

A single database can conceal semantic SQL errors; targeted test data can expose discrepancies missed by ordinary execution matching.

## Method

Agent-assisted development produces heuristic baseline-data generation and mutation-specific attack strategies, with occasional SMT use, schema-consistency repair and optional cross-checking pools. EX+ normalizes nondeterminism and compares successful query executions.

## Evaluation

A sanitized 36,042-pair suite compares refutation counts and tool runtime, with common-support and no-ordering subsets. Some benchmark failures informed implementation. Unseen checks include LargeJoin/TPC-H and ten BEAVER queries from one schema; the BEAVER outcome is non-empty-data generation, not pair refutation.

## What the results support

LASSO and pairwise cross-checking refute more pairs overall under the reported protocol. Broader cross-instance pooling yields smaller incremental gains at higher cost. The most effective attacks target table/join coverage, boundaries, grouping and null behavior.

## Limits and qualifications

Survival is not proof of equivalence. Sanitization, dialect conversion, ordering/type policies and supported features affect comparisons. Reported tool times exclude external dataset loading and query execution. Human oversight remained necessary to catch shortcuts; broad unseen-workload generalization is not established.

## Relevance to reliable Text-to-SQL

A practical counterexample generator and test-development study, not an NL-to-SQL accuracy metric or formal equivalence certifier.
